section.title: Introduction to Loops
section.content: Loops (or iterative structures) are control structures that allow the execution of a block of instructions to be repeated a certain number of times or until a condition is met. They avoid code duplication and are essential for processing data in bulk, traversing collections, or repeating calculations.

bulletPoints.point: ▶️ Allows actions to be repeated automatically without writing the same code multiple times.
🔁 Two main families: counted loops (known number of iterations) and conditional loops (repetition until a condition).
⚠️ Each loop requires a stopping condition to avoid infinite loops.
📥 Concrete example: display numbers from 1 to 10, calculate the sum of the first 100 integers, verify the validity of user input.

section.title: For Loop
section.content: The For loop is used when the number of repetitions is known in advance. It uses a counter that successively takes all values from an interval.

bulletPoints.point: 🔁 Syntax: For counter from start to end do instructions EndFor.
🔁 The counter is automatically incremented (by default by 1) after each iteration.
🔁 You can also specify a step (e.g: For i from 10 to 0 step -1 do ...).
📤 Example: display numbers from 1 to 5: For i from 1 to 5 do Display(i) EndFor → displays 1 2 3 4 5.
▶️ Example with negative step: For i from 5 to 1 step -1 do Display(i) EndFor → displays 5 4 3 2 1.
🎯 Usefulness: traverse array elements, perform a sum, a product, etc.

section.title: While Loop
section.content: The While loop executes a block of instructions as long as a condition remains true. The condition is evaluated before each iteration; if it is false from the start, the block is never executed.

bulletPoints.point: 🔁 Syntax: While condition do instructions EndWhile.
▶️ Warning: you must ensure that the condition becomes false at some point, otherwise the loop is infinite.
📤 Example: display numbers from 1 to 5 with While: i ← 1 While i <= 5 do Display(i) i ← i + 1 EndWhile.
🎯 Typical use case: repeat an action until a condition is met.
💻 Example: ask for a positive number: Read(n) While n < 0 do Display("Negative number, try again") Read(n) EndWhile.

section.title: Repeat Until Loop
section.content: The Repeat Until loop executes the block of instructions first, then checks the condition. It thus guarantees at least one execution.

bulletPoints.point: 🔁 Syntax: Repeat instructions Until condition.
💻 The condition is tested after execution; if it is true, the loop stops.
📤 Example: display numbers from 1 to 5 with Repeat: i ← 1 Repeat Display(i) i ← i + 1 Until i > 5.
📥 Ideal for interactive menus or user input.
📥 Example: input with validation: Repeat Read(n) Until n >= 0.

section.title: Nested Loops
section.content: You can place a loop inside another loop (nested loops). This allows traversing multidimensional structures or generating combinations.

bulletPoints.point: 🔁 Each level of nesting must have its own counter.
📤 Example: display a multiplication table: For i from 1 to 10 do For j from 1 to 10 do Display(i * j) EndFor Display(next line) EndFor.
💻 Example: traverse a 3x3 matrix: For i from 1 to 3 do For j from 1 to 3 do Read(matrix[i][j]) EndFor EndFor.
⚠️ Watch out for complexity: total number of iterations = product of loops.

section.title: Loop Control: break and continue
section.content: In some situations, you may want to prematurely interrupt a loop (break) or skip to the next iteration (continue).

bulletPoints.point: 🔁 Break: immediately exits the loop.
🔁 Continue: jumps directly to the next iteration.
🔁 In pseudo-code: "Exit" for break and "Skip" for continue.
🔁 Example with break: Found ← false i ← 1 While i <= N AND NOT Found do If array[i] = value_sought then Found ← true Exit EndIf i ← i + 1 EndWhile.
🔁 Example with continue: For i from 1 to 10 do If i % 2 = 0 then Skip EndIf Display(i) EndFor.

section.title: Common Pitfalls and Infinite Loops
section.content: Design errors can lead to infinite loops or unexpected behavior.

bulletPoints.point: ⚠️ Forgetting the increment.
⚠️ Badly written condition.
⚠️ Counter overflow.
❌ Loop that never executes.
🔁 Test with simple cases and verify the stopping condition.

section.title: Complete Examples of Algorithms with Loops
section.content: Here are several examples of algorithms using loops.

bulletPoints.point: 💻 Example 1: Sum of the first N integers Read(N) sum ← 0 For i from 1 to N do sum ← sum + i EndFor Display(sum)
📥 Example 2: Secure input Repeat Read(n) If n < 1 OR n > 10 Then Display("Invalid input") EndIf Until n >= 1 AND n <= 10
🧠 Example 3: Multiplication table Read(n) i ← 1 While i <= 10 do Display(n, " x ", i, " = ", n*i) i ← i + 1 EndWhile

🧠 Example 4: Prime number Read(n) If n <= 1 Then Display("Not prime") Else prime ← true i ← 2 While i * i <= n AND prime = true do If n % i = 0 Then prime ← false EndIf i ← i + 1 EndWhile If prime Then Display("Prime") Else Display("Not prime") EndIf

section.title: Best Practices for Loops
section.content: To write clear and efficient loops, certain best practices are recommended.

bulletPoints.point: ✔️ Choose the right loop according to the context.
✔️ Use explicit variable names.
✔️ Limit nesting.
✔️ Avoid overuse of break and continue.
✔️ Indent correctly.
✔️ Verify that the condition evolves.
